local players, and they will be forced to compete with those international
players who are not qualified yet (and usually have already had a chance to
qualify at their local qualifier).

> can host multiple qualifiers for it.

as unfair, but maybe they can have a qualifier where fewer (half?) players
qualify, and that will be enough to balance things.

So what you're saying is that you want to lure more players to the event

locals qualifying.

This should be filed under "Having your cake and eating it."

>Fewer players will be willing to make long journeys if they are to

Then regard the championship weekend as being for people who have
already qualified, and move on. A longer, two-day oriented format is
not impossible. See previous championships, where the championship
itself has been a separate style of tournament, combining sealed and
constructed play, over more than one day.

Alternatively, just hold another tournament the day before. Maybe a
sealed deck one, or a storyline one, or something, as appropriate. (You

qualifiers, so the locals get the chance to qualify twice somewhere
local?

Two tournaments - even if one of them attracts a chunk of players it
wouldn't normally - gives more chances for the same group of players to
qualify locally.

I don't think we can discuss this much further without actual stats from
qualifiers.

The idea is to find a balance, where local players can get around 8-10
qualification spots for themselves, to match the ones available to visiting
players in their local qualifiers.

For example, if there is a 50-50 split of local and visiting players in the
final qualifier, we might suppose the final table follows a distribution
that is somewhat equivalent to:

1 - Local
2 - Visiting
3 - Local
4 - Visiting
5 - Local
6 - Visiting
7 - Local
8 - Visiting
9 - Local
10 - Visiting
11 - Local
12 - Visiting
13 - Local
...

With 10 qualifications available, there will be 5 local players and 5
visiting players qualifying. If the top 5 local players have already
qualified, then you get 3 new qualifications for the local players, for a
total of 8. Note that in this case the visiting players also get a couple
extra qualifications. This seems rather reasonable. When considering that
some visiting players have already qualified too, there would be a small
adjustment resulting in a few more qualifications for local players.

Looking at the actual results from the 2002 Austrian Qualifier, I find that
the visiting players actually outnumber the locals by nearly 4:1.
In this case your analysis is nearly correct: if the Austrians had had a
previous qualifier with 5 spots available, and those who qualified there
were the 5 top best Austrian players at the EC Qualifier, they would've had
5 total qualifications, only one more than they actually had (4). That is
probably an improvement on the actual situation though.

This also means that if they had had a previous qualifier, with 10
qualification spots available, then they wouldn't qualify any extra players
at the final qualifier. So much for the 'unfairness' of having two
qualifiers in that case.

Note that at the 2003 EC only those 4 Austrians qualified. Many other
countries actually had more than 4 players participating, despite the
additional travel expenses.

Flux

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <b5q0ki$22j$1...@stu1id2.ip.tesion.net>, Andreas Nusser

<time...@NOSPAMscram.de> writes:
>Which I proposed in the first place. Refering to the Nation who hosts
>the EC this means that they would have a National Qualifier 3-5 months
>before and a Championship Qualifier the day before the actual
>championship!

This has already been noted as unfair, meaning that the locals get two
chances to qualify.

Why the pressing, urgent need to have an additional qualifier the day
before?

If there is a pressing, urgent need to get more people into the
championship, get White Wolf to allow more qualifiers. These do not
need to be local.

If there is a pressing, urgent desire to have a weekend of V:TES, you
could extend the tournament over two days. Even if you don't go for a
split format (e.g. sealed one day, constructed the next), it would not
be impossible to organise something like a 5 round qualifier. With 60
players (say), you should be able to organise enough distinct tables.
You would, of course, want to register decks for such an event, in the
event of organised cheating or accidental changes overnight. (The "Oh
shit, my card box fell open in my bag" accidents that happen to all of
us.)

If an extended tournament format like that is a problem, and we already
have enough people qualified, but we still want a weekend of V:TES so
that people don't just turn up for a day (which might be difficult from,
say, eastern Europe to Spain or Portugal, or similar items), there is no
need for the tournament the day before to be a qualifier. It's not
going to attract those who have *already* qualified to turn up, except
for it being an additional tournament to play in. They've already
qualified. They don't need to win.

If it's to attract people who *haven't* already qualified to turn up,
this doesn't have to be addressed on the day before, at the local
location. Making sure there are sufficient qualifiers planned would do
that. Or fiddling the number who come from each. We need 10 more
players? Well, make it the top 11 from each other qualifier. So that
might let 15-20 extra people in.

Indeed, if the idea is to provide people with other things to do, having
it as a qualifier may well exacerbate that problem. Extra, unqualified
people turn up on the Saturday. They play, they don't get through.
Their numbers may be relatively small, meaning that it's quite possibly
difficult to get a useful side-game going for them. Perhaps if only
half a dozen unqualified people turn up and stick around (locals have an
easier time going home, being less reliant on ferries, planes etc.), for
instance. Whereas with a *fun* tournament on the Saturday, everyone who
turns up on the Saturday internationally is already qualified, so they
won't be sat around twiddling their thumbs, and the unqualified locals
who turn up can treat it as a normal tournament - because it *is* a
normal tournament, that happens to attract a fair number of
international players also. And they get exactly the same chance to
qualify as everyone else, having a qualifier in their region.

I fail to see any pressing, overwhelming, soul-consuming need to have an
additional *qualifier* the day before.



"Johannes Walch" <johanne...@vekn.de> wrote in message news:<b5pjp1$7do$1...@stu1id2.ip.tesion.net>...
> > Just because you host the European Championships doesn't mean that you

> At the last EC in Vienna there was a lot of discussion about this subject
> and in the end almost everybody agreed to have an "international" qualifier
> the day before the event and a national qualifier way before the EC. There
> are several reasons to do it like this way (more players coming to the
> event, more players in the EC event) and almost none against, despite from
> the fact that it might be somehow "unfair".
>
> Anyway it has been discussed and decided (by Steve Wieck) so there is no
> need for more discussion. The majority of the players wants it to be this
> way and this is the best pro-reason of all.

Why would there be a problem prohibiting already qualified players
from playing in the "International Qualifier" the day prior to the
Championships? Since VTES tournaments of this caliber are typical 3+F,
one could argue that 3 rounds isn't enough to truly find the best
player, especially if there is potential for shenanigans by those with
invitations already. (In "that other game" a 7-round Swiss "Open
Qualifier" yields better results because there are twice as many data
points, as well as the "Swiss" function of the cream rising and
competing between themselves, unlike the VTES Recommended Seating
Chart)

It would seem that most "non-local" players attending the EC would be
making a last gasp attempt at qualifying. If they failed, they
travelled a long way and came up empty (though perhaps with a chance
to play in side events).

It would also give "locals" a chance to compete in an event with
mostly local players. If they succeed, they had a chance to represent
their location. If they fail, they can't gripe about having to compete
against a massive contingent of quality players who are gathered
primarily for another purpose, the Championship itself.

Last but not least, it would minimize any attempts at "collusion" by
those who qualified and those who hadn't since there would be no "out
of game considerations" to influence game decisions.

All these aside, I think a region should hold a separate qualifier
weeks in advance of the championships, as well as an International
Qualifier, strictly for those who have not yet qualified, the day
prior. Lots of professional sporting events do this sort of thing so
it's not such a big deal. As long as the venue for the Championship
rotates around, everyone will eventually get the big "bonus" of having
two "local" chances to qualify. Just make sure there's a major side
event available that is open to anyone and you'll get plenty of turn
out.

>After all, I personally know many people who just went to Vienna to
>visit the city and try the last chance qualifier. I don't know if they
>would have travelled without this possibility.

People travel for the qualifier, and the hope of getting into the final,
right?

So what we're saying is that if people think they might be in the
Championships, they'll travel?

How about you hold sufficient qualifiers before hand to have the number
of people you want qualified? Then those people who travel *know*
they're in the Championships.

Since you only have one Super Qualifier on the day before, you can only
add ten players *anyway*. Why not just have another 20-30 players
qualify around Europe instead?

This could be done by holding more qualifiers, allowing more people from
any given qualifier (top 11 or 12), shrinking some of the regions (as
some have pointed out, having more than one region in large countries
might be appropriate, handled sensibly) and so on.

If you need more people at the championships, have them qualify. If you
want a weekend of V:TES, have that.

Why the need, however, to qualify people on the day before?

Surely the people who travel in the random hope of qualifying would
travel if, uh, they were qualified already?

Why not have a 'wild card' qualifier saturday?

With 13 national qualifiers (as it happens to be this year) we can
assume that at least 120 players will qualify. Let's say that 60
of those actually preregister. You could have a last qualifier making
place for X% (for example 50) of the number of already qualified players
that haven't registered for the EC.

All players qualified at a national qualifier could be said to be
prequalified to the EC limited format held during saturday, which would
make it less likely that they would participate in the wildcard
tournament as they miss one EC tournament doing so.

I'm well aware that this "unjust" system will make more local players
participate in the end, but the last two decades to television watching
has proved to me that local troups tend to be overrepresentated at any
major, open, sportsevent anyway.

The main advantage with a system like this is that it helps raising the
opinion of the limited format.

Sten During
